subsystems.name: Retinoid payload
subsystems.role: the active molecule that improves skin turnover and collagen production but is unstable and irritating.

subsystems.name: Nanocarrier shell
subsystems.role: encapsulates the retinoid, protecting it from light and oxygen and controlling release.
parts: solid lipids or biodegradable polymers (PLGA, PCL)

subsystems.name: Aqueous dispersion
subsystems.role: carries the nanoparticles and forms the base of the serum or cream.

subsystems.name: Stabilisers
subsystems.role: prevent aggregation and chemical degradation during storage.

subsystems.name: Quality control
subsystems.role: verifies size, encapsulation efficiency and stability.

buildSteps.title: Dissolve the ingredients
buildSteps.detail: The retinoid and shell material (lipid or polymer) are dissolved in a small amount of organic solvent such as ethanol.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the water phase
buildSteps.detail: Purified water is mixed with surfactants and stabilisers to create the continuous phase.

buildSteps.title: Form the nanoparticles
buildSteps.detail: The two phases are combined and forced through a high-pressure homogeniser or sonicated to break the mixture into droplets tens to hundreds of nanometres across.

buildSteps.title: Remove the solvent
buildSteps.detail: The organic solvent is evaporated under reduced pressure or removed by dialysis, leaving solid nanoparticles suspended in water.

buildSteps.title: Purify and concentrate
buildSteps.detail: Ultrafiltration or centrifugation removes free retinoid and unwanted small molecules, and concentrates the nanoparticle suspension.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the batch
buildSteps.detail: Dynamic light scattering measures particle size (typically 50–200 nm), and HPLC checks how much retinoid is actually encapsulated.

buildSteps.title: Blend into the final product
buildSteps.detail: The nanoparticle suspension is mixed into a cream or serum base, with pH and viscosity adjusted for skin compatibility.

buildSteps.title: Test stability and release
buildSteps.detail: Accelerated stability tests (e.g. 40 °C for three months) and in vitro skin permeation studies confirm the retinoid stays encapsulated and releases as intended.

buildSteps.title: Scale up and fill
buildSteps.detail: Manufacturing moves to Good Manufacturing Practice conditions, and the product is filled into airless pumps to keep oxygen out.

prerequisites.why: liposomes and biodegradable polymer nanoparticles are already produced industrially for cosmetics and pharmaceuticals.
encapsulation slows degradation, but retinoids remain sensitive to light, heat and oxygen.
many chemical and physical methods exist to help nanoparticles reach deeper epidermal layers.
dynamic light scattering, zeta potential analysis and HPLC are standard tools for nanoparticle quality control.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory framework for nanomaterials in cosmetics
prerequisites.why: rules vary by country; some require extra safety assessment for engineered nanomaterials.

pathway.milestone: commercial products using liposomal or polymeric encapsulation of retinol
pathway.unlocks: reduced irritation and better stability for consumers.

pathway.milestone: stimuli-responsive nanocarriers that release retinoid in response to skin pH or enzymes
pathway.unlocks: targeted delivery to specific skin layers, maximising benefit and minimising side effects.

pathway.milestone: co-encapsulation of retinoids with other actives such as niacinamide or hyaluronic acid
pathway.unlocks: multi-functional skincare products from a single carrier.

pathway.milestone: personalised nanocarriers tailored to individual skin microbiome or genetics
pathway.unlocks: precision skincare with actives and release profiles matched to each person.
